title: Synthetic workload credentialing and customer acceptance playbook
creator: Raj Patel
description: Define and implement a tenant-aware synthetic workload "credentialing" system and an associated customer acceptance playbook for dedicated capacity throughput guarantees. The goal is to produce repeatable measurements that map to SLAs customers can sign against and to provide a clear runbook for onboarding customer validation runs.
background: Customers expect predictable throughput with Dedicated capacity contracts. Existing tools exercise fleet capacity but lack: (1) tenant-credentialed replay tokens tied to customer environments, (2) a canonical reporting template for signoff, and (3) a failure-mode taxonomy for autoscaler interactions. This ticket creates a single playbook combining a harness, methodology, and acceptance criteria.
scope:
- Implement a credential-based synthetic workload driver that can: provision per-customer test tokens, simulate realistic mix of short/long sequences, and inject KV-cache warmup phases.
- Define a benchmarking methodology that correlates ramp profiles to real-customer percentiles.
- Produce a customer-facing acceptance report template and automated dashboard snapshots.
- Integrate with autoscaler telemetry to validate policy behavior under controlled stress.
out_of_scope:
- Core autoscaler algorithm changes (separate RFC).
- Long-running chaos experiments unrelated to acceptance runs.
- On-prem private-install test deployment automation (handled by Private team separately).
proposal:
1) Credentialing: add a short-lived test credential model scoped to a customer tenant that the harness uses to annotate requests. This lets logs and billing maps show test runs separately.
2) Harness: build a modular load driver (python/Go) supporting scenario definitions (ramp, sustain, burst, tail) and tenant headers. Include a KV-cache warmup phase and deterministic RNG seeds for reproducibility.
3) Metrics and reports: standardize a CSV/JSON report with P50/P95/P99 token latency, throughput (tokens/s and reqs/s), error counts, autoscaler events, and resource utilization. Create a templated acceptance report for customer signoff.
4) Acceptance run checklist: preflight, run, post-analysis, signoff.
5) Safety gate: automated abort on >1% 5xx or on >2x expected memory growth.
benchmark_methodology:
- Scenario taxonomy: LIGHT (interactive chat), MIXED (chat + long-form generation), BULK (embeddings/large batch).
- For each scenario run: cold-start, warmup (10% of target duration), ramp to target over configurable window, sustain for 60 minutes, burst test of 10s peaks at 1.5x target throughput, cooldown.
- Measure token-level latencies and compute percentile envelopes over rolling windows.
- Correlate autoscaler decisions (scale events, scale latency) with tail-latency spikes.
- Repeat runs N=3 at staggered times to capture cluster noise.
- Produce normalized score: tokens/s per GPU and 95th tail latency per customer SLO class.
test_plan:
- Implementation tasks: instrument harness to emit structured tracing IDs, attach tenant test credential header, and publish run metadata to a central run-store.
- Preflight: validate credentialing, ensure no overlapping customer runs in same capacity pool unless explicitly allowed.
- Execute runs against a staging Dedicated fleet with traffic shaping to mimic noisy neighbors.
- Post-analysis: run automated scripts that compute report artifacts and compare to SLA thresholds.
- Customer acceptance: run the same harness from customer-owned bastion (optional) and produce mutual report for signature.
acceptance_criteria: Per-customer test credentials can be created and revoked and appear in audit logs.
Harness reproduces scenario taxonomy and produces standardized JSON/CSV report artifacts.
Automated dashboard snapshots (latency, throughput, autoscaler events) are generated and saved to the run-store.
For a targeted staging fleet configuration, runs demonstrate sustained throughput >= 95% of contractual tokens/s target while P95 latency remains within target bound in 3/3 repeatable runs.
Run aborts if errors exceed thresholds and a postmortem template is produced automatically.
Customer-facing acceptance report template vetted by PM and Legal and ready for customer signature.

risks: Test credentials could be misused if not properly scoped; must expire and be audited.
Staging fleet noise may not reflect heavy multi-tenant production characteristics; avoid overfitting the pass criteria.
Autoscaler interactions during synthetic stress could trigger cascading scale events if safety gates are not enforced.
Customer expectations around throughput guarantees must be aligned to measured scenarios to avoid SLA disputes.
